For each $\mu\in P$, $M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)_{\mu}$ is a free $\mathbb{A}$ -module and $\text{rank}_{\mathbb{A}}M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)_{\mu}=\dim_{\mathbb{C}(q)}M_{J}^{q}(\lambda)_{\mu}$.

5. Classical limits

In this section we take the classical limits of the $\mathbb{A}$ -forms of the quantum Verma-type modules, and show that they are isomorphic to the Verma-type modules of $U({\mathfrak{g}})$.

Recall that $\mathbb{A}=\mathbb{C}[q,q^{-1},\frac{1}{[n]_{q_{i}}},i\in I,n>0]$. Let $\mathbb{J}$ be the ideal of $\mathbb{A}$ generated by $q-1$. Then there is an isomorphism of fields $\mathbb{A}/\mathbb{J}\cong\mathbb{C}$ given by $f+\mathbb{J}\mapsto f(1)$ for any $f\in\mathbb{A}$. For any untwisted affine Kac-Moody algebra ${\mathfrak{g}}$, let $U_{\mathbb{A}}=U_{\mathbb{A}}({\mathfrak{g}})$, and set $U^{\prime}=(\mathbb{A}/\mathbb{J})\otimes_{\mathbb{A}}U_{\mathbb{A}}$. Then $U^{\prime}\cong U_{\mathbb{A}}/\mathbb{J}U_{\mathbb{A}}$. Denote by $u^{\prime}$ the image in $U^{\prime}$ of an element $u\in U_{\mathbb{A}}$. It was shown by Lusztig [Lu] and DeConcini and Kac [DK] that $(D^{\prime})^{2}=1$ and $(K_{i}^{\prime})^{2}=1$ for all $i\in I$. If we let $K^{\prime}$ denote the ideal of $U^{\prime}$ generated by $D^{\prime}-1$ and $\{K_{i}^{\prime}-1\ |\ i\in I\}$, then $\overline{U}=U^{\prime}/K^{\prime}\cong U({\mathfrak{g}})$, the universal enveloping algebra of ${\mathfrak{g}}$.

Note that, under the natural map $U_{\mathbb{A}}\to U_{\mathbb{A}}/\mathbb{J}U_{\mathbb{A}}\cong U^{\prime}$, we have $q\mapsto 1$. The composition of natural maps

$U_{\mathbb{A}}\to U_{\mathbb{A}}/\mathbb{J}U_{\mathbb{A}}\cong U^{\prime}\to\overline{U}=U^{\prime}/K^{\prime}\cong U({\mathfrak{g}}),$

is called taking the classical limit of $U_{\mathbb{A}}$.

Let $\overline{u}\in\overline{U}$ denote the image of an element $u\in U_{\mathbb{A}}$. Then $\overline{U}$ is generated by the elements $\overline{E_{i}},\overline{F_{i}},\overline{D}:=\overline{\left[\begin{matrix}D\ ;\ 0\\
\ \ 1\ \end{matrix}\right]}$ and $\overline{H_{i}}:=\overline{\left[\begin{matrix}K_{i}\ ;\ 0\\
\ \ 1\ \end{matrix}\right]}$, $i\in I$, and, under the isomorphism between $U({\mathfrak{g}})$ and $\overline{U}$, the elements $e_{i},f_{i},d$ and $h_{i}$ may be identified with $\overline{E_{i}},\overline{F_{i}},\overline{D}$ and $\overline{H_{i}}$, respectively. Further, Beck [Be1, Section 6] showed that we may identify the $\overline{E_{\beta}}$ with a PBW basis of $U({\mathfrak{g}})$, with elements denoted $e_{\beta}$.

For $\lambda\in P$, $J\subseteq\dot{I}$, let $M_{J}^{\prime}(\lambda)=\mathbb{A}/\mathbb{J}\otimes_{\mathbb{A}}M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)$. Then $M_{J}^{\prime}(\lambda)\cong M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)/\mathbb{J}M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)$ and $M_{J}^{\prime}(\lambda)$ is a $U^{\prime}$ -module. For $\mu\in P$, let $M_{J}^{\prime}(\lambda)_{\mu}=\mathbb{A}/\mathbb{J}\otimes_{\mathbb{A}}M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)_{\mu}$. Since $M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)=\oplus_{\mu\in P}M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)_{\mu}$, we must have $M_{J}^{\prime}(\lambda)=\oplus_{\mu\in P}M_{J}^{\prime}(\lambda)_{\mu}$. We also have the following standard result.

paper.title: Verma-type Modules for Quantum Affine Lie Algebras
paper.abstract: Let g be an untwisted affine Kac-Moody algebra and M_J(lambda) a Verma-type module for g with J-highest integral weight lambda. We construct quantum Verma-type modules M_J^q(lambda) over the quantum group U_q(g), investigate their properties and show that M_J^q(lambda) is a true quantum deformation of M_J(ł) in the sense that the weight structure is preserved under the deformation. We also analyze the submodule structure of quantum Verma-type modules.
